I fixed the failing test and pushed the fix to this branch in commit `05fa728`. `npm run check` now passes locally, with all 469 tests passing. I haven't seen the new CI run finish.

**What failed.** The one failing CI test was in `src/worktree.test.ts`: `WorktreeContinuity › doesn't restore into a checkout with uncommitted changes`. The system prompt changes in this PR didn't cause it. The bug was already in `captureState` in `src/storage/worktree.ts`, and it only shows up some of the time.

**Cause.** `captureState` copies `.git/index` to a temporary file, and the copy gets a new mtime. Git only re-reads a file's content when the file is at least as new as the index. Otherwise it trusts the size and mtime it saved. The test commits `file.txt` as `base\n` and then writes `pi's\n` right away. Both are 5 bytes, and on a fast runner both writes land in the same clock tick. So the size and mtime didn't change, and the newer copy made git skip the content check. The snapshot missed the change and saved nothing, so `restore()` returned `undefined`, which is the error in the CI log.

**Fix.** The copied index now keeps the real index's mtime, rounded down to the second. Git then still re-reads files that changed right after the index was last written. If the copy or the timestamp change fails, the code falls back to `read-tree` as before.

**New test.** I added a regression test to `src/storage/worktree.test.ts`. It makes this race happen every time by setting the file and index mtimes by hand and turning off git's ctime check (`core.trustctime=false`). It fails without the fix and passes with it.
